impact: ALLOWLIST entry 9's claim that the int/float distinction 'never affects a success-path byte' has two measured counterexamples: JSON token -0 renders as $-0.00 vs Python's $0.00, and cost fields are not safe-integer checked so an integral cost above 2^53 silently rounds. Both low-realism, neither worth a behaviour change alone. Entry 9 predates T-006, which owns only entries 13-15, so filed as ISS-008.
title: [allowlist-accuracy] ALLOWLIST entry 9's claim that the int/float distinction 'never affects a succes
